findings.title: Frontend (tss-grc-ui-v2) ships with zero executable automated tests and no test runner wired into the build
findings.cvss: High business risk (not a CVSS-scored vuln). The entire React/TypeScript SPA — auth flow, tenant-scoped data tables, RTL bilingual rendering, 200+ pages across 17 modules — has no executed regression net. Any refactor or dependency bump can silently break the only interface end users touch; defects reach production undetected because the sole automated check is type-checking, which proves nothing about runtime behaviour.
locations: tss-grc-ui-v2/package.json (devDependencies: no vitest, jest, @testing-library/* or playwright)
findings.description: The active frontend (tss-grc-ui-v2) is the production UI, yet it has no test runner installed and no executable test suite. package.json defines only four scripts — dev, build, preview, typecheck — and the devDependencies list (@types/*, @vitejs/plugin-react, typescript, vite) contains no test framework (no vitest, jest, @testing-library/react, or playwright). Two files exist under src/__tests__ (threeLines.test.ts, mobileCrisis.test.ts) but they import from Node's built-in node:test/node:assert and, per their own header comments, were written because 'The tss-grc-ui-v2 project has no test framework installed yet'. They are never executed by any npm script and are only fed through tsc --noEmit. So while two test FILES are present, the count of tests actually RUN in CI/build is zero. The only automated frontend signal captured in the audit is `tsc --noEmit` (audit/raw/tsc.log) which reported 0 errors — type correctness, not behavioural correctness — and a 6-case Playwright smoke suite that lives OUTSIDE the repo in audit/artifacts/e2e (it covers login happy/sad path and screenshots only, not module CRUD, validation, tenant scoping, or workflow transitions).
findings.rootCause: No testing dependency or `test` npm script was ever added to tss-grc-ui-v2; the v1 static UI (tss-grc-ui) likewise has none. Component, hook, and integration testing was deferred ('once a runner is added', per the test-file comments) and never picked up. CI therefore gates the frontend on type-checking alone.
findings.evidence: audit/raw/tsc.log: `tss-grc-ui-v2@0.1.0 typecheck` / `tsc --noEmit` (clean, 0 errors). package.json scripts block contains no "test" entry; devDependencies = [@types/node, @types/react, @types/react-dom, @types/sockjs-client, @vitejs/plugin-react, typescript, vite] — no test framework. `find tss-grc-ui-v2/src -iname '*.test.*' -o -iname '*.spec.*'` => 2 files, both using node:test and unrunnable by the project toolchain. No vitest.config.* / jest.config.* present. Backend, by contrast, runs 1858 JUnit tests (audit/raw/mvn-test.log, 174 surefire reports, 0 failures/0 errors/0 skipped).
findings.impact: Regressions in authentication, multi-tenant data display, bilingual/RTL layout, form validation, and workflow UI ship undetected. There is no guard against breaking changes during dependency upgrades (e.g. React/Vite/Bootstrap bumps) or refactors. Frontend defects are caught only by manual QA or in production. Given the platform is bilingual + multi-tenant, subtle locale/tenant bugs are exactly the class of error unit/component tests catch cheaply and humans miss.
findings.reproduction: 1) `cd tss-grc-ui-v2 && cat package.json` — observe no `test` script and no test framework in devDependencies. 2) `npm test` — fails / no-op (no script). 3) `cat src/__tests__/threeLines.test.ts` — header states there is no test framework; it imports node:test. 4) Confirm the only CI signal is `npm run typecheck` (tsc --noEmit), which passed with 0 errors but executes 0 assertions.
findings.resolution: Adopt Vitest + @testing-library/react + jsdom (Vite-native, minimal config). Add a `test` script and a `coverage` gate. Convert the two existing node:test files to Vitest. Prioritise: (1) auth/session helpers and the API client (token handling, 401 refresh), (2) the i18n/RTL switch, (3) per-module list/detail pages with mocked API responses, (4) form validation. Add Playwright as a committed e2e dependency (the audit's external 6-case suite proves the app is automatable) and expand beyond login to module CRUD and tenant-switch flows. Target an initial 40% line coverage gate, rising per sprint.

findings.title: Backend branch coverage is 26.0% and 762 of 1324 classes (57.6%) have 0% coverage — decision logic is largely unexercised
findings.cvss: High quality risk. 1858 passing tests give false confidence: only 26% of branches and 22.3% of cyclomatic complexity are exercised, and over half of all classes are never touched at runtime by any test. Conditional logic — exactly where defects and security checks live — is the least-covered dimension. Untested error paths, validation branches, and authorization decisions can regress without any test turning red.
findings.description: JaCoCo (computed from tss-grc-backend/target/site/jacoco/jacoco.csv over 1324 classes) reports: LINE 38.5% (17,324 covered / 27,728 missed), INSTRUCTION 37.1% (93,819 / 159,128), BRANCH 26.0% (5,308 / 15,079), METHOD 31.9% (2,656 / 5,667), and COMPLEXITY (cyclomatic) just 22.3% (4,203 / 14,636). Branch and complexity are the weakest, which is the worst dimension to be weak in: branches are the if/else, switch, ternary, and exception decisions where logic errors hide. Aggregating per-class, 762 of 1324 classes (57.6%) have ZERO instruction coverage — no test ever loads them. Notably, several classes carrying confirmed Critical/High findings sit at 0%: AuthController (SEC-AUTH-001), EvidenceMatrixService (Critical PERF-NQ-003 + High QUAL-IE-001), DataOfficerService (QUAL-ESG-001), OtAssetService (Critical SEC-CYB-002). The 1858-test count is real and all pass, but it is concentrated in service happy-paths; whole layers (controllers, integration glue, error handling) are dark.
findings.rootCause: Tests are predominantly Mockito unit tests on service classes covering nominal flows. Controllers, exception handlers, validation branches, and many newer modules were never given tests. There is no enforced coverage gate (no JaCoCo `check` rule failing the build below a threshold), so coverage drifted down as modules were added faster than tests.
findings.evidence: jacoco.csv aggregate: BRANCH covered=5308 missed=15079 => 26.0%; COMPLEXITY covered=4203 missed=14636 => 22.3%; INSTRUCTION 37.1%; LINE 38.5%; METHOD 31.9%. Per-class scan: 762/1324 classes at 0% instruction coverage. Vulnerable-class coverage sample — AuthController 0%/0%/0% (instr/branch/line), EvidenceMatrixService 0%/0%/0%, DataOfficerService 0%/0%/0%, OtAssetService 0%/0%/0%, BcmService 25%/43%/31%, CyberService 44%/55%/45%, EvidenceItemService 60%/36%/61%. Test totals from surefire: 1858 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped across 174 classes (audit/raw/mvn-test.log).
findings.impact: High-complexity, low-coverage classes are the most likely to harbour latent bugs and to regress silently. Because branch coverage is 26%, most conditional paths — including authorization checks, tenant-scope guards, status-transition guards, and error handling — are never asserted. A change that flips a condition (e.g. removes a tenant predicate, as in several confirmed IDOR findings) will not fail any test. Refactoring the 0%-covered god-services (DataOfficerService 1000+ lines, OutsourcingService) is effectively unguarded.
findings.reproduction: 1) Open tss-grc-backend/target/site/jacoco/jacoco.csv and sum BRANCH_COVERED / (BRANCH_COVERED+BRANCH_MISSED) => 0.260. 2) Count rows where INSTRUCTION_COVERED=0 and INSTRUCTION_MISSED>0 => 762. 3) Filter those rows by CLASS ending 'Controller' => 201 fully-uncovered controllers. 4) Grep AuthController / EvidenceMatrixService rows => 0 across all metrics.
findings.resolution: Introduce a JaCoCo coverage gate in pom.xml that fails the build below a floor and ratchets up over time (e.g. start at line 38% / branch 26% — current levels — then +2% per sprint). Prioritise the 0%-coverage classes that carry findings or high complexity: write branch-focused tests for AuthController (login success/lockout/refresh-rotation), EvidenceMatrixService (matrix build + N+1 path), and the god-services. Track branch coverage specifically, not just line, in CI reporting.
findings.patchBefore:
<!-- tss-grc-backend/pom.xml — jacoco plugin used for report only, no gate -->
<plugin>
  <groupId>org.jacoco</groupId>
  <artifactId>jacoco-maven-plugin</artifactId>
  <executions>
    <execution><goals><goal>prepare-agent</goal></goals></execution>
    <execution><id>report</id><phase>test</phase><goals><goal>report</goal></goals></execution>
  </executions>
</plugin>
findings.patchAfter:
<!-- tss-grc-backend/pom.xml — add a ratcheting coverage gate -->
<plugin>
  <groupId>org.jacoco</groupId>
  <artifactId>jacoco-maven-plugin</artifactId>
  <executions>
    <execution><goals><goal>prepare-agent</goal></goals></execution>
    <execution><id>report</id><phase>test</phase><goals><goal>report</goal></goals></execution>
    <execution>
      <id>coverage-gate</id><phase>verify</phase><goals><goal>check</goal></goals>
      <configuration><rules>
        <rule>
          <element>BUNDLE</element>
          <limits>
            <limit><counter>LINE</counter><value>COVEREDRATIO</value><minimum>0.38</minimum></limit>
            <limit><counter>BRANCH</counter><value>COVEREDRATIO</value><minimum>0.26</minimum></limit>
          </limits>
        </rule>
      </rules></configuration>
    </execution>
  </executions>
</plugin>

// Example: cover AuthController login branches (0% -> exercised). Uses MockMvc with security.
@SpringBootTest @AutoConfigureMockMvc
class AuthControllerIT {
  @Autowired MockMvc mvc;
  @Test void login_success_returns_token() throws Exception {
    mvc.perform(post("/api/auth/login").contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
        .content("{\"username\":\"admin\",\"password\":\"Admin@12345\"}"))
       .andExpect(status().isOk())
       .andExpect(jsonPath("$.accessToken").exists());
  }
  @Test void login_bad_credentials_returns_401() throws Exception {
    mvc.perform(post("/api/auth/login").contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
        .content("{\"username\":\"admin\",\"password\":\"wrong\"}"))
       .andExpect(status().isUnauthorized());
  }
}

findings.title: Confirmed Critical/High security findings have no test asserting the vulnerable path — 5 of 6 Critical findings sit on classes at 0% coverage or with tests that miss the exploit
findings.cvss: High. The test suite gives no protection against the platform's most serious confirmed defects. Of the 6 Critical security findings in audit/crit_high.json, 3 sit on classes with NO test file at all and the other 3 have a *Test.java that exercises only nominal paths, never the cross-tenant/SQLi/mass-assignment exploit. There is therefore no regression net: a future fix could be reverted and every test would still pass. This is the gap that lets IDOR/BFLA findings persist undetected.
locations: tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/ccm/runner/CustomSqlRunner.java (SEC-INT-001 Critical — test exists but only checks DML rejection, not cross-tenant SELECT)
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/cyber/service/CyberService.java (SEC-CYB-001 Critical — test exists, no cross-tenant assertion)
tss-grc-backend/src/main/java/com/tss/grc/module/bcm/service/BcmService.java (SEC-BCM-001 High — test covers plan tenant-scope but NOT the vulnerable BIA path)
findings.description: Cross-referencing every Critical/High Java finding in audit/crit_high.json against the 174 backend test classes shows the suite does not exercise the vulnerable code paths. Of 6 Critical findings: SEC-CYB-002 (OtAssetService mass-assignment), SEC-FIN-001 (IntakeController unauthenticated PII leak), and SEC-IAM-001 (ApprovalChainController approval forgery) have NO corresponding *Test.java and their classes are at 0% JaCoCo coverage. SEC-INT-001 (CustomSqlRunner cross-tenant SQL exfiltration) has CustomSqlRunnerTest, but reading it shows 8 tests that only verify INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/chained-statement REJECTION and threshold logic — none asserts that a legitimate SELECT (e.g. `SELECT * FROM iam.users`) is constrained to the caller's tenant; indeed the source has no organisation/tenant predicate at all. SEC-CYB-001 (CyberService IDOR) has CyberServiceTest (14 tests) that stub repos with the caller's own ORG_ID and never simulate an attacker requesting another org's id. The clearest example is SEC-BCM-001: BcmServiceTest DOES contain tenant-isolation tests (getPlan_other_tenant_throws_EntityNotFound, invokePlan_other_tenant_throws) for the BcmPlan path — proving the team knows the pattern — yet the High finding is on the BIA path (updateBia/deleteBia at BcmService.java:221-236 call biaRepo.findById(id)/deleteById(id) with NO tenant scope), and there is no test for createBia/updateBia/deleteBia or any cross-tenant BIA assertion. The defensive test pattern exists but was simply never applied to the vulnerable method.
findings.rootCause: Security-negative test cases (attacker requests another tenant's id; SQLi payload; mass-assignment of a foreign id) were not written. Tests assert what the code does on the happy path, not what it must refuse. Controllers carrying authorization findings have no MockMvc/security-context tests, so missing @PreAuthorize annotations are invisible to the suite.
findings.evidence: Automated cross-reference (audit/crit_high.json x src/test): Critical findings missing any *Test.java => OtAssetService, IntakeController, ApprovalChainController (all 0% JaCoCo). BcmService.java:221-232 updateBia / 235-237 deleteBia call `biaRepo.findById(id)` and `biaRepo.deleteById(id)` with no TenantContext predicate; BcmServiceTest method list contains getPlan_other_tenant_throws_EntityNotFound and invokePlan_other_tenant_throws_EntityNotFound but ZERO methods referencing bia/createBia/updateBia/deleteBia (grep 'bia' => only the @Mock field). CustomSqlRunnerTest (115 lines, 8 tests): insertIsRejected/updateIsRejected/deleteIsRejected/chainedSelectIsRejected/threshold tests only — no cross-tenant SELECT test; CustomSqlRunner.java has 0 matches for 'organisation|tenant|TenantContext'. CyberServiceTest: all repo stubs use ORG_ID (the caller's own org); no OTHER_ORG/forbidden/cross-tenant case.
findings.impact: The most severe confirmed defects (cross-tenant data theft, unauthenticated PII exposure, approval forgery, SQL-driven exfiltration) are completely unguarded by automated tests. When these are remediated, nothing prevents a later change from re-introducing them. Conversely, until remediated, the green test suite actively masks their existence and gives auditors/management false assurance.
findings.reproduction: 1) `python` cross-reference: for each finding in audit/crit_high.json, derive ClassNameTest.java and check existence in src/test => OtAssetService/IntakeController/ApprovalChainController have none. 2) Read BcmServiceTest.java — confirm tenant tests exist only for plan, none for BIA; read BcmService.java:221-237 — confirm biaRepo.findById/deleteById are unscoped. 3) Read CustomSqlRunnerTest.java — confirm only DML-rejection tests; read CustomSqlRunner.java — confirm no tenant predicate. 4) Read CyberServiceTest.java — confirm all stubs use the caller's ORG_ID with no foreign-org case.
findings.resolution: Add a security-negative test for every Critical/High finding, co-located with the fix, asserting the exploit is now refused. Pattern: arrange a record owned by OTHER_ORG, set TenantContext to ORG_ID, assert EntityNotFound/AccessDenied. For controllers, use @SpringBootTest + MockMvc + @WithMockUser to assert 403 for unauthorized roles and isolation across tenants. Mirror the existing BcmServiceTest plan-tenant pattern onto the BIA path. For CustomSqlRunner, assert a SELECT against a foreign tenant's rows is blocked (after adding a tenant guard / read-only constrained datasource). Make these tests part of the regression gate so the findings cannot silently return.
references: OWASP ASVS v4 V4.1 (Access Control), V5.3 (SQLi), V1.14 (CI verification)
CWE-639 (IDOR), CWE-862 (Missing Authorization), CWE-915 (Mass Assignment), CWE-89 (SQLi)

findings.title: Authorization is untested end-to-end: 201 of 231 controllers (87%) have 0% coverage and only 4 tests use MockMvc — BFLA findings are invisible to the suite
findings.cvss: Medium-to-High. The eleven 'Broken Function Level Authorization' findings in audit/crit_high.json (controllers gated only by isAuthenticated() or missing @PreAuthorize entirely) cannot be caught by the current suite because controller tests instantiate the controller with @InjectMocks and call methods directly, bypassing Spring Security. Only 4 of 174 test classes wire MockMvc/SpringBootTest, and none target the vulnerable controllers. Authorization correctness is therefore asserted nowhere.
findings.description: The platform exposes 2175 endpoints across 231 controllers, but only 28 controllers (12%) have a *ControllerTest, and JaCoCo shows 201 of those 231 controllers (87%) at 0% coverage. More importantly, the EXISTING controller tests do not test authorization: the representative pattern (e.g. ObligationControllerTest) uses `@Mock` for the service and `@InjectMocks` for the controller, then calls controller methods as plain Java — Spring Security, the @PreAuthorize layer, and the JWT/tenant filter are never in the loop. Only 4 of 174 test classes reference MockMvc/SpringBootTest/WebMvcTest/@AutoConfigureMockMvc (CoiControllerTest and the three integration-webhook controller tests), and 19 reference @WithMockUser. Crucially, NONE of those security-aware tests cover the eleven BFLA findings (PolicyController, ControlMapController, CloudServiceController, GhgEmissionRecordController, AttachmentController, ConsentRecordController, NdiAssessmentCycleController/NdiAuditController, LicensingController, AutomationRuleController, SupplierResilienceController). Because authorization is enforced by annotations resolved at the Spring proxy/filter layer — not in the method body — a missing or wrong @PreAuthorize is structurally invisible to @InjectMocks-style tests. The suite can be fully green while every BFLA hole is open.
findings.rootCause: Controller tests were written as plain unit tests (service mocked, controller called directly) rather than as MockMvc slice/integration tests that route through Spring Security. No convention exists for asserting @PreAuthorize / role gates / tenant isolation at the HTTP boundary. The bulk of controllers have no test at all.
findings.evidence: jacoco.csv: 231 classes ending 'Controller'; 201 at 0% instruction coverage. `find -name '*ControllerTest.java'` => 28. `grep -rlE 'WebMvcTest|MockMvc|SpringBootTest|@AutoConfigureMockMvc' src/test` => 4 files (CoiControllerTest, CrowdStrikeControllerTest, ServiceNowControllerTest, TenableControllerTest). `grep -rlE 'WithMockUser' src/test` => 19. ObligationControllerTest header: `@Mock private ObligationService service; @InjectMocks private ObligationController controller;` (no MockMvc, no security). Endpoint total 2175 across 231 controllers per audit facts.
findings.impact: The platform's authorization model is unverified at runtime. Adding, removing, or mis-scoping a @PreAuthorize on any of 2175 endpoints produces no test failure. This is the direct cause of the BFLA findings going undetected in development. For a multi-tenant GRC product where tenant isolation and least-privilege are core selling points, having zero HTTP-level authorization tests is a material assurance gap.
findings.reproduction: 1) `find tss-grc-backend/src/test -name '*ControllerTest.java' | wc -l` => 28; `find tss-grc-backend/src/main -name '*Controller.java' | wc -l` => 231. 2) `grep -rlE 'MockMvc|SpringBootTest|WebMvcTest' tss-grc-backend/src/test | wc -l` => 4. 3) Open ObligationControllerTest.java — confirm @InjectMocks direct-call style, no security. 4) jacoco.csv => 201/231 controllers at 0%.
findings.resolution: Establish a MockMvc-based authorization test convention. For each controller, add a security slice test asserting: (a) anonymous => 401, (b) authenticated-but-wrong-role => 403, (c) correct role => 2xx, (d) cross-tenant id => 404/403. Start with the controllers carrying BFLA findings, then expand. Consider an automated guard test that scans all @RequestMapping handler methods and fails if any write/delete endpoint lacks a @PreAuthorize (reflection-based meta-test) to prevent regressions across all 2175 endpoints cheaply.
references: OWASP API Security Top 10 — API5:2023 Broken Function Level Authorization

findings.title: End-to-end coverage is a 6-case external smoke suite (login + screenshots only); business workflows and module CRUD are untested e2e
findings.cvss: Low-to-Medium. The only browser-level automation that exists is a 6-test Playwright smoke suite living outside the repo (audit/artifacts/e2e), covering login happy/sad path, a demo-skip bypass, session persistence, and a11y/responsive screenshots. It does not exercise any module's create/read/update/delete, workflow state transitions, tenant switching, or bilingual data entry. The integrated stack — frontend calling the 2175 backend endpoints under real auth — is essentially unverified by automation.
findings.description: A Playwright run captured in audit/raw/playwright.log executed 6 tests, all passing (1.1m): E2E login success -> /risk, login failure -> error shown, demo-skip bypass navigates without auth, session persists across reload, plus an a11y+screenshots pass across key pages and a responsive mobile-screenshots pass. This suite lives in audit/artifacts/e2e (an audit-time scaffold), not in tss-grc-ui-v2, so it is not part of the project's committed build and would not run in the team's CI. Functionally it is a thin smoke test: it proves the app boots, login works, and pages render for screenshotting — it asserts nothing about creating a risk, advancing a workflow (e.g. the 9-step cyber incident state machine), submitting a BIA, switching tenants, or rendering Arabic/RTL data correctly. Combined with FUNC-001 (no committed frontend unit tests) and FUNC-004 (no HTTP authorization tests), there is no automated check that the integrated system behaves correctly for any real user task beyond logging in.
findings.rootCause: E2E testing was set up only as an audit artifact, not adopted into the repo. No page-object structure, no per-module scenarios, and the suite is not wired to any npm script in tss-grc-ui-v2. The 'demo-skip bypass navigates without auth' case being a passing test also hints at an intentional auth-bypass affordance that itself warrants review.
findings.evidence: audit/raw/playwright.log: 'Running 6 tests using 1 worker ... 6 passed (1.1m)'; test titles = login success->/risk, login failure, demo-skip bypass navigates without auth, session persists across reload, a11y + screenshots across key pages, responsive mobile screenshots. Suite location: audit/artifacts/e2e/tests/audit.spec.ts (single spec file) with its own package.json/playwright.config.ts under audit/artifacts/e2e — outside tss-grc-ui-v2. tss-grc-ui-v2 has no playwright dependency or e2e script.
findings.impact: Integration regressions — broken API contracts between the SPA and the 2175 endpoints, workflow transition bugs, tenant-scope leaks visible only through the UI, RTL/locale data defects — are not caught automatically. Manual QA is the only safety net for full user journeys. The e2e harness exists but delivers near-zero functional assurance beyond authentication.
findings.reproduction: 1) `cat audit/raw/playwright.log` — observe 6 tests, all smoke/login/screenshot. 2) `ls audit/artifacts/e2e/tests` => single audit.spec.ts; confirm it lives outside tss-grc-ui-v2. 3) `grep -i playwright tss-grc-ui-v2/package.json` => no match (not a committed dependency).
findings.resolution: Promote the Playwright harness into tss-grc-ui-v2 (add @playwright/test devDependency and an `e2e` script). Build a small page-object layer and add critical-journey specs per module: create+list a risk, run an evidence review four-eyes flow, advance a cyber incident through its state machine, switch tenants and assert data isolation in the UI, and toggle EN/AR asserting RTL + Arabic field rendering. Run e2e against a seeded DB (seed_real_data.py) in CI nightly. Separately, security-review the 'demo-skip bypass' that navigates without auth — ensure it is dev-only and cannot reach production.
